text: Yes, the property did lose tree cover in 2019. Observations from Hansen's Global Forest Change data (GFC-2025-v1.13 and GFC-2019-v1.7) indicate a tree-cover loss event of 1.8 hectares (0.05% of the asset) in that year. This loss was corroborated by the JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 data, which mapped the entire event area as forest in 2020. Additionally, the Uruguay Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries' national forest cartography confirmed that the area was planted forest, specifically Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda.
